I've described my experiences with converted Buck 110s, one of my favorite autos of all time. Some are quite nice and worth every penny, others not so much, depending upon who did the work.

Here's something to keep in mind when you see them offered for sale at $125 a piece:

http://www.dhgate.com/product/buck-110-traditional-hunting-knife-double/256593529.html

If you look around on this site you'll see some amazing-looking bargains on name brand knives, sometimes being offered for little more than 20% of the usual retail price.

My understanding is that there are basically three sources for these items:

1) Some are just knock-offs, look-alike copies made of cheaper materials.

2) Some are seconds. Many name-brand knives are made in China, and a fraction of these fail quality inspection. They are supposed to be destroyed, but many are basically just stolen and resold.

3) Some are deliberate overruns. Once a production line is set up and running, most of the difficulty and expense is behind you, and the price of running an additional batch of knives is quite low, little more than the cost of raw materials. Again, it's illegal, but it's China and these things happen fairly often.

The buyer never knows. An overrun knife is basically a real name-brand knife that has been stolen and resold. A second will be defective, in a way that might be obvious, or might not. A knock-off might be anything, but will surely be something inferior.

I've heard (correctly or not) that Buck has never made the 110 overseas, so these knives are almost certainly just knockoffs, designed and built from the ground up as auto instead of being converted after the fact. They are not bad at first glance, but they can be prone to dangerous failure - an inexpensive, soft brass pin resting in a dimple on the blade is the only thing holding it closed, and that pin gets worn a little more every time the knife is opened and closed.

Buck makes their own automatic knife now, the 898 Impact, but they have always said they would not make an automatic version of the 110. I'm sure they have their reasons, and probably very good ones, too, but it does seem a shame.
